# What a Calendar App Needs

A calendar app lets users create, view, and manage time-based events. This document outlines the core requirements across functionality, data, integrations, and quality attributes.

## 1. Core Features

### Event Management
- **Create, read, update, delete (CRUD)** events with a title, start/end time, location, description, and attendees.
- **All-day events** that span one or more days without a specific time.
- **Recurring events** with rules such as daily, weekly, monthly, or custom patterns, plus the ability to edit or delete a single occurrence or the whole series.
- **Reminders and notifications**, including configurable lead times (e.g., 10 minutes, 1 day before) and support for multiple alerts per event.

### Calendar Views
- **Day, week, month, and agenda (list) views**, with navigation between periods.
- **Multi-calendar support**, letting users organize events into separate calendars (e.g., Work, Personal) with distinct colors and visibility toggles.
- **Search and filtering** by title, attendee, location, or date range.

### Scheduling Essentials
- **Time zone handling** — events must store an unambiguous point in time and display correctly across time zones, including daylight saving changes.
- **Conflict detection** — warn users when a new event overlaps an existing one.
- **Availability and free/busy lookup** (for apps with scheduling features).
- **Invitations and RSVP** — send invites, receive responses (accepted/declined/tentative), and update attendees on changes.

## 2. Data Requirements

| Need | Purpose |
|---|---|
| Canonical event data model | Consistent storage of times (UTC or offset-aware), recurrence rules (e.g., RRULE), and metadata |
| iCalendar (RFC 5545) support | Interoperable import/export of events |
| Stable event IDs and revision tracking | Reliable synchronization and change detection |
| Local storage/cache | Fast rendering and offline access |

## 3. Integration and Sync

- **Two-way synchronization** with major providers (Google Calendar, Outlook/Exchange, Apple Calendar).
- **CalDAV support** for standards-based server sync.
- **Push or near-real-time updates** so changes from other devices or attendees appear promptly.
- **Shareable calendars** — subscribe to external calendars (holidays, team schedules) and share calendars with granular permissions.

## 4. Quality Attributes

- **Offline-first behavior** — view and edit events without a connection; reconcile changes on reconnect.
- **Performance** — fast rendering of dense views (e.g., a month with hundreds of events) and lazy loading of distant date ranges.
- **Reliability** — never silently lose or duplicate events; handle sync conflicts deterministically.
- **Security and privacy** — encrypted transport and storage, per-calendar access control, and minimal data collection.
- **Accessibility** — keyboard navigation, screen reader labels, sufficient color contrast (especially for calendar color-coding).

## 5. Platform Considerations

- **Cross-device consistency** — the same event data on mobile, web, and desktop.
- **OS integration** — system notifications, widgets, and "add to calendar" hooks from other apps.
- **Responsive layout** — views that adapt from phone-sized screens to large desktop monitors.

## Minimum Viable Set

If prioritizing, the indispensable baseline is: event CRUD, recurring events, time zone correctness, reminders, multiple calendars, day/week/month views, and reliable sync with at least one major provider.
